newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine brokers upbeat at U.S. vote results.
newsitem.headline: Argentine brokers upbeat at U.S. vote results.

text.p: The outcome of the U.S. presidential election should help Argentina's bolsa keep a steady tone well into 1997, brokers said.

"It's exactly the kind of division of power that keeps the markets happy," said trader Luis Diaz at Medefin-UNB bank, referring to the re-election of U.S. President Bill Clinton and the continued Republican control of Congress. But the blue-chip MerVal index .MERV bucked the trend on Wall Street Wednesday, falling 0.7 percent to 579.60 midsession compared with a rise of nearly one percent in the Dow Industrials.
Traders shrugged off the fall as a normal precaution.

"It's the classic case of 'buy on the rumor, sell on the fact'," said Diaz. "But even if there's a downward correction here I'd say we're on a medium-term upward course, because U.S. yields are low and they're even starting to talk of a U.S. interest rate cut now, instead of a hike."
Analysts said the new Clinton administration might bring other good news.

"It will be interesting to see whether in the second term the Clinton administration moves closer to Latin America, which so far hasn't been very high on its agenda," said an analyst at a foreign investment bank. "Each change of government brings at least a slight change of focus and the possibility exists that Latin America will become a bigger priority, which would indirectly benefit the bolsa."

On the home front, traders noted that political rows over corruption charges were fading and had not made a serious dent in prices. And they were hopeful economic recovery would continue while tax revenue slowly starts to pick up.

"The economic outlook looks fairly stable, with no clouds on the horizon," said Augusto Marinozzi, head of equity research at Mildesa bank. "The rate of direct investments remains good and, while I wouldn't say I'm overly bullish long-term, I do think we're recovering a sense of optimism after a negative patch."

The MerVal rose 10 percent in September and 2.6 percent in October, but has failed to reclaim this year's high of 617.55 set July 26. Daily floor volume has also shrunk considerably since peaking at 53 million pesos early January.
Traders said labor reforms, if passed by the end of the year by Congress, could underpin the market. But international cash flows remained the most important factor.

"With yields shrinking abroad, investors are looking for gems in the emerging markets," said Diaz. He singled export driven sectors and companies, such as oil-based holdings and steelmakers, as choice picks on the bolsa.
